episode_title: S2E21 - Mark Sturdy: Using Technology to Enhance the Customer Experience

real_qa.q: How does Adrenaline Group distribute sports streaming content to pubs and venues in Australia?
real_qa.r: Adrenaline Group secured an IP platform with fit-for-purpose commercial distribution that covers 2,000 venues. The platform allows broadcast rights owners to put sports from streaming platforms like Paramount Plus into local pubs. The technology stack enables consumers to watch content like the Matildas and Socceroos in venues without realizing it's coming through Adrenaline's technology infrastructure.
real_qa.requete: Adrenaline Group sports streaming pubs venues

real_qa.q: What gap in the sports broadcasting market did Adrenaline Group identify and address?
real_qa.r: As sports fragmented from traditional free-to-air broadcasters to players like Optus Sport, Stan Sport, Paramount, Netflix, and Amazon, none of these streaming platforms had a fit-for-purpose solution for commercial distribution at scale into venues. Adrenaline identified that pubs and sports bars had no path to get streaming products onto their screens despite paying six-digit figures annually for sports licensing.
real_qa.requete: streaming platforms commercial distribution venues problem

real_qa.q: How does Adrenaline Group create shared value between venues, consumers, and advertisers?
real_qa.r: Instead of venues only seeing sports licensing as an outgoing expense, Adrenaline enables them to generate revenue by commercializing the screen real estate. Brands connect with fans in sports bars through targeted local advertising—national brands can localize campaigns to individual dealers or any local business can advertise in specific venues, creating visibility opportunities at lower costs than stadium advertising.
real_qa.requete: sports bar advertising revenue shared value model

real_qa.q: What is Adrenaline Edge and how does it support product startups?
real_qa.r: Adrenaline Edge is a secondary business that works with startups and product creators to identify which products are viable and scale them to market. Rather than startups bearing the full cost and risk of sales and marketing, Adrenaline Edge partners with them to handle sales, marketing, and scaling based on commercial terms where everyone wins. This addresses the challenge that many startups face: the high cost to scale even when they have exceptional products.
real_qa.requete: Adrenaline Edge startup scaling product launch

real_qa.q: How does Adrenaline Group use AI without emphasizing it as a product feature?
real_qa.r: Adrenaline deliberately started lean nine months ago and automated processes with AI first before hiring roles to fill gaps. From a product-to-consumer perspective, AI is invisible infrastructure—it delivers sports analytics, breaking news, and other content automatically without the customer needing to know it's AI-powered. The company views AI as a pipe that delivers the product, not as a badge to add value for marketing purposes.
real_qa.requete: AI invisible product consumer experience automation

guest.bio_context: Mark Sturdy acquired the core assets of Adrenaline Group on December 1, 2025, from a previous business where he was working. He has extensive experience in the venue space including stadiums, race clubs, sports bars, and licensed venues across Australia. He built a solid advisory board of three skilled individuals and assembled a core team with whom he has worked for many years, deliberately starting lean and leveraging AI to automate processes before filling gaps with hired roles.

real_quote: We don't see AI as a product that the consumer needs to know it's AI. It could just be automatic. It's just the pipe that actually delivers the product to the customer.
key_stats: Adrenaline Group founded December 1, 2025 (9 months old as of episode)
2,000 venues covered by the IP platform partnership
Pubs pay six-digit figures annually for sports licensing costs
Started with three-person advisory board to guide business decisions
Deliberately began as lean startup to test AI automation before hiring staff
